derived_threshold.robustness_note: Derived from only 3 sub-threshold groups with a fitted coefficient that is non-positive (Si_O n=0 fitted=0.0 exactly; vinyl_CH2 n=31 fitted<0; nitrile n=124 fitted<0) against 21 positive-fitted groups in a 24-group table -- a small-sample boundary, not a statistically powered generalization bound. The empirical gap between the highest excluded n_train (124, nitrile) and the lowest included n_train (154, carbonyl) is wide enough ([125, 154) contains no observed data points) that any threshold value in that gap (125 through 154) yields the IDENTICAL 15-included/9-excluded partition, so the exact choice of 125 vs. e.g. a rounder 150 is immaterial to which groups are in/out. This threshold should be revisited if Phase-1 adds training polymers for the excluded low-support groups.

method: Self-contained re-derivation from the ridge-fit KPI's own fitted_Ygi_comparison array (24 rows, each already storing n_train_polymers_with_group, fitted and published Y_gi). Sign-admissibility per group is defined as Y_fitted_K_g_per_mol > 0 (the published table is 100% positive by Van Krevelen 1990 / Bicerano 2002 convention, so a positive fitted coefficient is the physically-consistent direction). The per-group training-support threshold is derived, not assumed: T = 1 + max(n_train_polymers_with_group) over every group whose fitted Y_gi is NOT sign-admissible in this dataset (this includes the two W8 sign-flipped groups, vinyl_CH2 n_train=31 and nitrile n_train=124, and the zero-support Si_O row n_train=0 whose fitted coefficient is identically 0.0 and therefore undetermined, not merely small). This is the tightest data-derived boundary above which every group in the actually-observed 24-group table is sign-consistent -- it is read directly off the failure boundary in the data rather than picked as a round number.

supersedes.reason: W8 (2026-08-03) REFUTED this KPI's headline claim that the fit 'confirms the 24-group structure is correct' / 'resolves' the prior under-determination hypothesis: 2/24 fitted Y_gi are sign-reversed vs the published (100% positive) baseline, both in the bottom third of per-group training support. R-A09 recorded REFUTED status in RETRACTION-INDEX.md; B3 retracted the mission.md prose asserting structural correctness but left 'scope-limited to groups with n_train of roughly 500 or more' as an unimplemented placeholder recommendation, not an actual per-group re-scoping of the KPI's own claim_locks. This receipt performs that re-scoping: it derives a training-support threshold directly from the KPI's own stored per-group table (not assumed as 500), partitions the 24 groups into in-scope / excluded, restricts the surviving structural-correctness claim lock to the in-scope groups only, and names the excluded ones.

why: The original (unscoped) claim remains REFUTED and is NOT reinstated by this receipt -- W8's finding stands, reconfirmed live this fire by byte-identical re-execution of its own script. What this receipt adds is a properly re-scoped claim: restricting '24-group structure confirmed correct' to the 15 groups with n_train_polymers_with_group >= 125 (a threshold derived from the data's own sign-admissibility boundary, not assumed), all 15 of which are sign-consistent with the published Van Krevelen table (0 flips found when the original W8 pre-registered criterion is re-applied restricted to this subset). The 9 excluded groups (nitrile, F, vinyl_CH2, ester, Br, sulfone, Cl, sulfide, Si_O) include both original W8 sign-flips (vinyl_CH2, nitrile) plus 6 further groups whose n_train (0-32-ish range... see per_group_table) is below the empirical admissibility boundary and are therefore not asserted as structurally confirmed either, pending more training data. Honesty caveat retained: sign-consistency is NOT the same as small magnitude error -- 6 of the 15 in-scope groups still deviate >50% in magnitude from published (already disclosed by the original KPI as expected calibration drift, not re-litigated here).
